page: OVHcloud t1-le-180 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated cloud instance designed for parallel computing and machine learning workloads. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, the server delivers 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs without hyperthreading. System memory totals 180 GB of RAM, providing 5.62 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs offering an aggregate of 64 GB VRAM. The instance includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps running under KVM virtualization.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented heavily toward hardware-accelerated computation rather than raw host CPU speed. LLM inference benchmarks demonstrate top-tier execution across small, medium, and large model sizes, with prompt processing on a 70B parameter model reaching 146.99 tokens per second and 7B model generation attaining 112.23 tokens per second. Conversely, host CPU single-core performance registers in the lower quartile across stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations, reflecting the conservative base clock and IPC of the Xeon Silver family. Multi-core CPU operations, memory bandwidth, and Redis throughput remain within average performance tiers.

From an infrastructure perspective, the four-GPU configuration yields dense compute density for matrix operations and parallelized model execution. The Volta architecture represents a legacy accelerator generation that provides a cost-effective alternative to newer enterprise GPUs for workloads that fit comfortably within the 16 GB per-card memory boundary. Tradeoffs include modest local NVMe storage capacity and lower single-thread CPU performance, necessitating external storage architectures for large datasets. The instance is best suited for distributed deep learning inference, model fine-tuning, computer vision processing, and GPU-intensive mathematical simulations.
